items.title: Drinking in the Moonlight

items.title: Coffer
items.summary: Il coffer è un'opera attribuita ad André-Charles Boulle, attivo in Francia nel periodo di Luigi XIV. Realizzato principalmente in quercia e con inserti preziosi come tartaruga, ottone dorato e bronzo dorato, rappresenta un esempio significativo dell'arredamento francese del XVII secolo. La sua produzione fu commissionata da importanti figure reali e aristocratiche.

art.medium: Oak, tortoiseshell, brass, gilded copper, gilded bronze, pewter, ebony, and oiled paper

items.excerpt: Coffer. Attributed to André-Charles Boulle (born France, 1642–1732) Paris. c. 1700–20. Oak, tortoiseshell, brass, gilded copper, gilded bronze, pewter, ebony, and oiled paper. The cabinetmaker André-Charles Boulle was responsible for some of the finest examples of French furniture made during the reign of Louis XIV (1643–1715).

items.title: Of Old Sat Freedom on the Heights
items.summary: La poesia descrive una figura femminile associata alla libertà, che si erge su cime rocciose e ascolta il suono delle cascate. Sebbene ispirata e profonda, la sua voce si disperde nel vento, invitando a un'esplorazione della verità e del desiderio di conoscenza.
items.titleIt: Di Vecchie Libertà sulle Cime
items.excerpt:
Of old sat Freedom on the heights,
The thunders breaking at her feet:
Above her shook the starry lights:
She heard the torrents meet.
There in her place she did rejoice,
Self-gather'd in her prophet-mind,
But fragments of her mighty voice
Came rolling on the wind.
Then stept she down thro' town and field
To mingle with the human race,

He is best known for advancing "British Emergentism", a movement that held mind "emerges" from matter.

items.titleIt: Relatività: Una Poesia di Henry Twells
items.excerpt: Fixed to the front of the clock case in the north transept of Chester Cathedral is a poem by Henry Twells (1823–1900): When as a child I laughed and wept, Time crept. When as a youth I waxed more bold, Time strolled . When I became a full grown man, Time RAN. When older still I daily grew, Time FLEW . Soon I shall find, in passing on, Time gone . O Christ!
